chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Abdillah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Sandal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj and Dawud ibn Farqad (both) from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: We asked him

about a man who has wealth belonging to orphans, and he does not give it to them until they die, then their heir and their agent come to him, and he makes a settlement with him to take some and leave some, and to acquit him of what he would have acquitted him of. He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.يُصَالِحُهُ: he makes a settlement/compromise with him

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for an heir or agent of orphans when the guardian delays distributing the orphans' wealth until their death?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *sulh* (amicable settlement) in the management of orphan's wealth, allowing the guardian to retain a portion as compensation for delay or mismanagement when the heir agrees. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding financial accountability, where the right to claim the full amount can be waived through mutual consent, reflecting the practical needs of estate administration.
